title: NeoRadar holds
description: data/holds.geojson in a vAcc's sector source, beside topsky/ and euroscope_data/: the vAcc's holding patterns, a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (RFC 7946, WGS84 longitude and latitude) with one Point feature per hold at its fix. Field names follow AIXM 5.1 HoldingPattern where it has one. `neoradar-cli convert` checks it against this schema and carries it in server-dataset.json under `holds`; nothing of it goes in the package. Optional: no file means no holds are served. Written once by an importer (`neoradar-cli import-ukcp`) or by hand; the vAcc's copy is the master after that. Not expressible here and checked by `convert`: hold ids unique, and every `separatedHolds` entry names another hold of the file. A hold whose lower limit is above its upper limit is warned about and carried.

$schema.description: Editor hint only. `neoradar-cli convert` drops it.

sources.description: Where the facts in this file came from, one entry per source. A GeoJSON foreign member.

name.description: What the facts were taken from: a document, a file or a data set.

url.description: Where that source can be found.

version.description: The edition, commit, AIRAC cycle or date of the source as read.

licence.description: The source's licence, where it states one. Only facts are taken from a source; no code or text.

notes.description: Anything the author should know about what was taken and how.

icao.description: An ICAO location indicator, four letters or digits, upper case.

holdId.description: A hold's id, unique in the file: lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens.

uom.description: FL: a flight level, `value` in hundreds of feet. FT: feet, read as a controller reads a hold table, an altitude where it is at or below the transition altitude at the hold and the flight level of that many feet above it (7000 above a 6000 ft transition altitude is FL70).

fix.description: The designator of the fix the hold is at, as the sector file names it.

name.description: The hold's name as a controller knows it (LAM, LOGAN (High), BIG).

usage.description: What the hold is for. Absent: not stated.

servesAirports.description: The airports whose traffic the hold is for. Absent: not stated.

outboundLeg.description: The outbound leg, as a time or a distance. Absent: the standard timing for the level.

lowerLimit.description: The lowest level of the hold.

upperLimit.description: The highest level of the hold.

speedLimitKt.description: Indicated airspeed limit, knots. Absent: the standard limit for the level.

minimumLevels.description: Rules that keep the lowest usable level of the hold above an airport's live transition level. A level is unusable when any rule that applies refuses it.

blockedLevels.description: Levels never assigned in this hold.

separatedHolds.description: Holds deemed separated from this one.

insertDistanceNm.description: Two aircraft at one level, one in each hold, are deemed separated only while more than this far apart, nautical miles.

published.description: False for a hold not in the AIP.

aircraft.description: Which aircraft may use the hold.

minimumLevel.description: Read in order: when `whenRunway` is written and that runway is not in use, the rule refuses nothing; else a level below `floor` is refused; else, while the airport has a transition level, a level below it plus `plusLevels` thousands of feet is refused.

rule.description: The airport's live transition level (data/altimetry.json `airfields`) is the base. In the UK that is the minimum stack level (MSL).

plusLevels.description: Thousands of feet above the transition level (UK: MSL+1 is 1).

floor.description: A level the rule refuses anything below while it applies, whether or not the airport has a transition level.

whenRunway.description: The rule applies only while this runway of the airport is in use.

use.description: In use for what: `any` is either.
